rationale: Sulpiride (selective D2/D3, no sedation, high prolactin, renal excretion) to quetiapine (broad receptor profile: D2, 5-HT2A, H1, M1, α1/α2; moderate metabolic risk; antidepressant augmentation via norquetiapine). Common reasons: bipolar depression requiring mood stabilisation with quetiapine's antidepressant profile, desire for insomnia management, or reducing prolactin. Sulpiride withdrawal is generally well tolerated — no significant anticholinergic rebound. Quetiapine initiation brings sedation, postural hypotension, and metabolic risk. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start quetiapine 100 mg nocte. Continue sulpiride 800 mg. Record baseline metabolic parameters. Warn about postural hypotension on quetiapine initiation.
Increase quetiapine to 200 mg nocte. Plateau sulpiride.
Increase quetiapine to 400 mg (target). Reduce sulpiride to 400 mg. Prolactin will begin to fall as sulpiride reduces.
Reduce sulpiride to 200 mg. Quetiapine well established. Monitor metabolic parameters.
Stop sulpiride. Continue quetiapine 400 mg. Metabolic monitoring at 4 and 12 weeks.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sulpiride 800 mg ≈ quetiapine 400 mg (via DDD and CPZ equivalence proxy). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
